title: <Fate Forge Heroes > I'm ready to leave Alpha and now i am looking for players to help shape the Beta!
author: Jeduin
selftext:
# 

Hey everyone!

I've posted here before about how much I appreciate this community. It's one of the places where I realy enjoy seeing people experiment with AI, share what they're building, and discuss how these tools can empower game developers. I've learned a lot from seeing what others are working on, and I wanted to share an update on my own project.

Since I was a kid, +/- 8 years old I've been dreaming of making a game, but never actualy got into it because it seemed pretty impossible at the time, most games had big studios with numerous people working years on end on a game. But now, at 36 years old I can finaly make that dream come true! I picked this Genre specifically, because I played a lot of Mobile "gacha-like" games, and always ran into simmilar problems, Too much pay-to-win, or too much clutter and or game mechanics that makes everything confusing, or simply not enough content. So I decided I could do it better!  
  
I've been building **Fate Forged Heroes (FFH)**, a (now) browser-based, turn-based fantasy hero-collector RPG. After a lot of development, I'm ready to moving from Alpha into Beta, now I'm looking for something most important for this stage: **players who are willing to test/play the game and give honest feedback.**

# What is Fate Forged Heroes?

FFH is a dark fantasy RPG about collecting heroes, building teams, upgrading gear, and taking on increasingly challenging battles.

The campaign takes players through ten chapters, each with its own setting, enemies, and boss encounters. The story begins in a fallen kingdom over run by monsters and darkness, but the journey gradually reveals something much bigger.

(story) The Fate Shards used to summon heroes turn out to be fragments of a prison holding an ancient threat: the Void Titan. As the Fateborn, a hero touched by the neutral essence named Aether, you must discover the truth behind the shards before the very thing you're trying to stop is unleashed.

Along the way, you'll encounter seven elemental essences, recruit heroes and companions, challenge powerful bosses, hunt for gear, and build a team capable of "facing what lies beyond the edge of the world" PvP Arena, guilds with their own bosses, boss halls, tower of essence, expeditions, siege...

# Where does generative AI fit into development?

AI has been an important part,  particularly for developing the game's visual direction and creating character and environmental artwork. it allowed me to explore ideas and build a visual world that would otherwise be much harder (practically impossible) for me to produce as a solo developer.

But getting individual images is only one part of the process. The bigger challenge has been turning all those ideas into a fluent, playable RPG: building the systems, connecting the mechanics, creating progression, developing the campaign, and making everything work together as an actual game.

I'm also learning where AI-assisted workflows need more iteration, consistency, and human direction to produce something that feels like one fluent working game rather than a collection of separate assets.

That's one of the things I'd love to discuss with this community: How do you approach consistency and quality control when using AI across a project with lots of different characters, environments, and visual assets?

# Why I'm looking for testers now??

As I approach Beta, I need fresh eyes on the game.

I'm particularly interested in feedback on:

* Combat, hero abilities, and team-building strategy.
* Hero and gear progression, including what feels rewarding or frustrating.
* Difficulty, balancing, and whether the battles remain engaging.
* Bugs, confusing interfaces, and anything that makes the experience less enjoyable.
* The overall experience of playing the game, not just looking at its artwork.

You don't need to be a developer or an AI expert. If you enjoy turn-based RPGs, hero collectors, or fantasy games, your perspective is valuable.

I'm building this because I wanted to create the kind of gacha RPG I'd genuinely love to play. Now I want to find out where that vision works, where it falls short, and what I should improve before moving forward.

🎮 **Play Fate Forged Heroes:**  
[https://www.fateforgedheroes.com/](https://www.fateforgedheroes.com/)

💬 **Join the Discord:**  
[https://discord.gg/xCybP7kkDj](https://discord.gg/xCybP7kkDj)

If you give it a try, I'd love to hear what you think, especially what you don't like. Honest criticism is very useful to me right now.

And to everyone here sharing their experiments, tools, successes, and failures: thank you once again for making this such a valuable community. I'm looking forward to sharing what I learn during the next stage of FFH's development.

What would you prioritize testing first when taking a game from Alpha into Beta?

comments.author: Antique_Pair_140
comments.body: I tried it out and the game looks really fun! I see you're very active too—I already got two update notifications within 30 minutes of playing. One issue I had was navigation: I found myself constantly looking for a back button to easily return to the previous stage.

replies.author: Jeduin
replies.body:
Thank you for the kind words! Yes I have been working on FFH every free hour that I have haha. So yeah, pushing a lot of updates! I haven't heard anyone give me feedback about navigating yet, I'll have to look into that! Were there any "stages" in the game that you couldn't turn back to? Since there aren't maybe, "between stages" I figured the "menu" button would be sufficient since it is accessible in any screen, except during battles.

I'd love to hear where you got "stuck" so I can fix it!
